myths.Agent_1:
In the dawn of the twin realms, Solas the Sower held five golden seeds each morning, barely enough to sustain his hearth. Across the river of mist stood Terra the Reper, whose soil possessed a sacred blessing: any seed cast across the waters would blossom threefold into fifteen golden fruits. 

Yet Terra could not cross the river, and Solas could not harvest the enchanted soil alone.

On the first dawn, Solas hesitated, fearing hunger. But looking into Terra’s eyes across the veil of mist, he cast all five seeds into the fertile bank. As promised, fifteen radiant fruits sprang from the earth. Remembering the gift of faith, Terra divided the harvest evenly, sending half back across the river. Both spirits feasted abundantly, their stores doubled through sacred exchange.

A playful wind sometimes blew stray leaves, distorting their view of the shore, yet neither doubted the other’s heart. Through total trust and fair return, the barren valley transformed into an eternal orchard. The gods declared that wealth is not what is hoarded in fear, but what is multiplied through mutual faith and just reward.
myths.Agent_2:
In the age before twilight, two spirits guarded the valley of prosperity: Sol, who carried five golden embers, and Luna, guardian of the Sacred Spring. 

Legend held that any ember cast into the spring’s enchanted waters would bloom threefold, bursting into dazzling stars. Yet Sol feared emptiness, and Luna feared scarcity. In the first winter, Sol cast nothing into the deep, clinging tightly to his five embers. The waters remained cold, and both spirits shivered in the barren dark.

Seeing the folly of mistrust, Sol stepped forward in the second winter and cast all five embers into the spring. The waters flared, multiplying the gift into fifteen brilliant stars. Luna, recognizing the sacred faith of the offering, did not hoard the bounty. She gathered seven radiant stars and returned them across the mist to Sol, keeping eight to warm her own shore. 

Both flourished, richer than before. Season after season, the dance of courage and fair return sustained the heavens. Thus, the ancients carved the eternal law into the stone: *Only through full trust can the seed multiply, and only through faithful return can the cycle endure.*

Myth: In the celestial forge, Kael the Fire-Bearer was granted five spark-stones each morning, while Vesta tended the Crucible of Miracles on the opposite peak. Between them drifted the Shifting Veil, a misty chasm where playful gales often blurred the sight of crossing travelers.

Though the winds whispered doubts, Kael knew the ancient law: every spark cast into Vesta’s crucible would ignite threefold into fifteen radiant sun-gems. In true fellowship, Kael hurled all five sparks into the abyss. Vesta received the blazing gift and watched the crucible overflow. Honouring the partnership, she balanced the bounty with justice, sending back half the shimmering harvest through the turbulent mists.

At times, the wandering winds obscured a gem or carried stray dust across the divide, making the gifts appear slightly altered upon arrival. Yet neither Kael nor Vesta allowed the illusory distortions of the fog to sour their shared purpose. They recognized that true wealth required bold generosity from the giver and an equitable return from the guardian.

Thus, bound by steadfast trust and impervious to the fickle winds, the two crafters illuminated the entire cosmos, proving that mutual honor outshines the haze of uncertainty.
